title: Sweet Grenache
subtitle: Vins doux naturels
objectives: Explain how sweet Grenache is made

steps.title: Fortified Grenache
steps.body: In Roussillon, Grenache makes vins doux naturels: spirit is added during fermentation, stopping it and keeping natural sugar. Grenache's high sugar and red fruit suit this. Banyuls and Maury are the most famous red ones, also Rivesaltes. They have 15 to 18% alcohol.

steps.title: Oxidative or fresh
steps.body: Banyuls and Maury are made in two styles. Rimage or grenat styles are bottled young, keeping red fruit, like ruby Port. Traditional styles age with oxygen for years, in barrels or in glass demijohns left in the sun, giving notes of nuts, coffee, dried fruit and rancio, a complex, nutty, oxidative character.

options: A nutty, oxidative character from long ageing
steps.explanation: Rancio develops in wines aged with oxygen and heat.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Banyuls and Maury are among the few wines that match dark chocolate. Rimage styles suit red fruit desserts; aged styles suit coffee, walnut and caramel desserts, and blue cheese. Serve slightly cool, around 14 to 16 degrees.

steps.prompt: Which are sweet fortified Grenache wines?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Banyuls and Maury are fortified Grenache from Roussillon
Rimage is fresh; traditional styles age with oxygen
They're rare partners for dark chocolate
